author: nbcbayarea
title: Audit highlights concerns regarding body cameras worn by Palo Alto PD officers
text:
A newly released independent audit highlighted concerns about body camera compliance within the Palo Alto Police Department.
A newly released independent audit highlighted concerns about body camera compliance within the Palo Alto Police Department, as auditors found several incidents where cameras were not properly activated.
Ali Reid reports.
“Body worn cameras are gamechangers when it comes to our auditing responsibilities and often are determinative in deciding whether or not the officers’ conduct was consistent with policy,” said Michael Gennaco with Oir Group. That role of body cameras is now at the center of an independent audit, reviewing officer misconduct complaints and use-of-force cases completed earlier 2026.
“We found several situations in which for one reason or another the body worn camera did not depict all of the encounter or one of the officers on scene did not appropriately activate his or her body worn camera,” Gennaco said. The report recommended that the department strengthen training to ensure interactions are properly recorded. Palo Alto's police chief says the incidents reviewed occurred largely during the first half of 2025.
“In none of the cases were the officers found to have done anything inappropriate in the way they handled the call for service and more importantly, in none of the cases was there an absence in footage of the incident,” Chief James Reifschneider said. The department says officers now conduct camera checks before every shift and recently completed a transition to newer body cameras.
“We think that this new camera that we have moved to will have better functionality, better battery reliability,” Reifschneider said. Auditors note they found no evidence officers intentionally failed to record encounters. Still, they say camera activation remains an area requiring continued attention.
“Our recommendation is that the department should redouble its efforts in regards to training, maintenance and interventions to make sure that there is a record,” Gennaco said. The audit and the department’s response will ultimately be presented to the Palo Alto City Council later this year. Auditors say they’ll revisit the issue in future reviews to see whether compliance improves.
